Our Team Won the Daytona track for the AGI, Inc. x OpenAI x LOVEABLE for warmscreen, an agentic interview agent (with many features, lie detection, voice cloning and avatar plus much more). extended TL/DR: Intended as a B2B from inception, with copious use cases like catching lies in an interview, to potentially catching outliers perfectly candidates that might be filtered out, agentic interviews allow any candidate to interview…and as I found out warmscreen is a great way to learn and train for interviews! The inital build started with 36,000 lines of code, we had about 24 hours to get our MVP working as intended. The Key Learn- perseverance! Compute lagged, hardware broke and we needed to ship. All with a massive codebase that needed to be integrated into the front end. This akin to eating the grocery store for dinner, ambition lead the charge. So there we were, submission time…perseverance take the lead. The MVP was configured(more than minimal, as the interview agent performance is bananas!), demo recorded and ahhh moment. What we can build and ship today is Shocking- the tools and support is unprecedented! Build times have never been this fast for things that have never been built! I am always stunned by the other submissions. Ode to Humility and Awe of Emergent Tech. At this moment let us think about Fast, Scalable, Stateful infrastructure for AI agents. Enter Daytona! Run in a sandbox without risk to your infrastructure, no doubt this will continue to come into play as we continue to build automation with self learning, self healing systems. Build, Fix, Evaluate. Thank you Irina Mira Human-In-The-Loop, and Abhay Rathi ML and data for being the core team. Big shout out to my friends who also jumped in on this one🤍🙌🏼🏆🙌🏼 I was curious how this project would run from the initial, minimal yet highly effective one-shot. Usually I follow up with a mega prompt to formalize the inital build. The one shot build spawned 7 tooled agents, we had mis en place - and need to serve three stars. Cook Time! We had to pivot and serve- thank you AGI, Inc. , Daytona, and Colin Lowenberg/ Frontier Tower for the most host! Absolutely Love What We Built using Agentic General Intelligence! Having been passionately devoted towards save AGI/ASI since transformers entered the chat, it is awesome to link up with CK and the AGI team to serve it up on the bleeding edge. Build Responsibly and Persevere! ...more ...more

Cerebral Valley Gemini VibeCode Hackathon professional photos signify the significance of ideation. We are gathered to build, create and share ideas that form the human technological interactions. Here we stand at the forefront of emergent tech, learning these wears, ideating, creating and pondering monitization to carry the load. At this event our team Abhay Rathi rolled in, ideas forming like nimbostratus, determined to use the Gemini AI Studio exclusively for the build, I and others hit backend build challenges. Mine specifically on certain errors. Here many use their trusted tools. I stuck with the studio, determined, solve for error, solve for error…My typical work flow has solved this path after over a year of T/E, with new emergent model usage this now works. However determined to stick with the tool in hand, I made a pivot. Split and build a safety. Speaking with another attendee, who said with determination, I always think of how my product will sell first and I am looking for someone to build (X). I built this project (X), shared/collab the repo. The safety, a project to spin up and submit, simple enough to complete MVP+Demo in time was built. Our team divided, still working on both projects. I completed (X), and Loved it. So much so I used it the next day at the Uncanny Valley hackathon YC, where I got my invite half way though that event, although Abhay Rathi always gets his invites to YC immediately, cracked. In conclusion, notes from the hackathoner, ideas are shared, given, morphed, the best products may rise to production , or may never be seen! Ideas may be taken by other and transformed into a fully monitized product. There is a fever thirst for creativity, ideas; and high pressure faucets yearning to port into projects and yeild fields of abundance. Here is the field of potential connectivity. All while we fumble with new toys, seeking to transform them into a product with the perfect price. Try. Learn. Adapt. There will be no path here and we may need to jump. Rise Era of the Leaper. ...more ...more

Four American hard tech companies raised $3.68 billion inside four days. JPMorganChase took part in three of them. What the capital is funding: Hadrian - $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, running automated factories that make parts for missiles, submarines, and spacecraft. Base Power Company - $1B Series D at $13B post-money, up from $4B ten months earlier, installing home batteries that feed the grid back. Valar Atomics - $1B Series B led by Sequoia at a reported $6B, after its reactor powered an Nvidia Blackwell chip. Mariana Minerals - $310M Series B led by Khosla Ventures at $1.5B, running a Utah copper mine and a Texas lithium project on its own software. JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group anchored Hadrian's round, co-led Base Power's, and the bank sat in Valar's $200 million credit facility. That group operates inside a $1.5 trillion, ten-year program built around defense, energy, critical minerals, and frontier technology. Venture firms priced software while banks financed the physical economy. Both are now writing into the same round at the same company, and that combination is what makes a factory or a reactor financeable at venture speed.

What does real transformation actually look like inside an organization? I asked Kavitha Mariappan , Chief Transformation Officer at Rubrik , this during our conversation on The O'ChakDe Show , and I really liked her take. 💯 It’s not just about new technology or big innovation initiatives. Sometimes it’s much simpler: give people the right tools to do their jobs and get rid of the stuff that slows them down, like outdated systems, technical debt, unnecessary processes, and the classic “we’ve always done it this way.” That last part stuck with me. How often do we actually stop and question whether there’s a better, faster way to get to the outcome we want? Great perspective from Kavitha . 🎙️ Check out the full episode in the comments below 👇 #Leadership #Transformation #Innovation #Excellence #Rubrik

I've been pretty quiet about this while we've been building. But we reported Q2 today, and Brian said on the call that AI is the best thing to ever happen to Airbnb, so it feels like the right moment to share what that's looked like. When we built grocery delivery last year, it took about nine months. Airport pickups, launched recently, took six weeks. Same quality bar. That's now the pattern across the company: concept-to-launch time down as much as 60% on key initiatives, and nearly 80% more features and improvements shipped in the first half than the same period last year. One decision I'd highlight: we never measured AI adoption by usage. Plenty of companies spent this year mandating AI and counting tokens. We measured throughput, what ships and whether it's good. Usage took care of itself. We’re just getting started. There’s a lot more coming across search, discovery, recommendations, support and the host experience as we push AI deeper into the product. And we continue to aggressively shift our momentum towards small teams, moving fast, with agents that can carry entire workflows. The goal is simple: make Airbnb feel more intuitive, more personalized and easier to use for our community. I'm really proud of the team. A shift like this doesn't come from a model release, mandate or a new tool (or even a new CTO). It comes from thousands of engineers willing to change how they work, all at once, without lowering the bar. The momentum is real, and the best part is how early we still are. https://lnkd.in/gNzuzSgY

A year ago, I probably would’ve laughed if you told me I’d be spending my summer trying to build a new approach to computing. But here we are. Excited to share that I’ve joined Entrepreneur First’s San Francisco fellowship program to continue building Sumeru Quantum! At Sumeru, we’re exploring a new approach to computing using superconducting digital logic, with the goal of building significantly more energy-efficient compute infrastructure for AI and HPC. We’ve been moving quickly from architecture to hardware, developing circuit-level simulations, designing our first superconducting test structures, and working toward fabrication and experimental validation. Along the way, I’ve had the opportunity to work with and learn from researchers and engineers across superconducting electronics, fabrication, and high-performance computing. Excited for what’s ahead 📈

I just hired my first secretary. He Works 24/7. Never complains. Costs me $200 a month. Its name is Claude Cowork. Here is what it actually runs for me thats makes it so valuable to me: Study plan. I gave it everything I want to learn this year. It built the whole plan, the materials, the practice questions. Morning check in at 10am, night check in at 10pm, where I tell it what I did, what I learned, and what I didn't. If I fall behind, it reshuffles my calendar around it. Formula 1. Every weekend it gives me a full brief on the grand prix, the teams, how each car is set up and what every driver said in their interviews. Morning brief. I wake up, ask it what I have today, and it pulls my calendar, my emails, my GitHub, and any news I need to know. Inbox and calendar. Sending, replying, scheduling. It handles it whenever I'm too lazy to do it myself. Health. Connected to my Apple Watch, so it tracks my calories and my training and tells me if I'm actually hitting my fiber goal by taking pics of when I'm eating through my meta ray bans. Content. Every week or two I export my social medias data into it and it tells me what's working and which mistakes I keep repeating. Three to four hours a day back. Things that used to eat an afternoon now take twenty minutes. It starts at $20 a month on Pro. I pay $200 because I run it all day. More people should be doing this.

As a business school professor, I’m always urging my students to set clear goals, make a plan, be ambitious, and be intentional. I often remind them: “You can’t get anywhere if you don’t know where you’re going.” Well....sometimes life has other plans. Exactly three months ago, a freak accident left me with a fractured ankle and five broken metatarsals in my foot. Surgery followed, along with two months in a cast, then a boot, unable to walk. Suddenly, things I had always taken for granted - walking, climbing stairs, showering, driving, traveling - became impossible. I became dependent on others in a way I had never experienced before, and those first two months were incredibly difficult. It was a stark reminder that, despite our best intentions, life doesn’t always go according to plan. We can set goals and chart a course, but we also have to learn to adapt, accept what we cannot control, and appreciate what we often take for granted. Fortunately, I can now walk without a cane - and it feels wonderful! Looking forward to the start of the semester in less than two weeks - I’ll keep telling my students to have a destination in mind, but perhaps with one addition: be prepared for life to change the route. A Big Thank You to my family and friends for their kindness and support. Special shout out to Tara , Shanker and Nikhil !
